To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conformation of goat peripheral blood lymphocytic lectin is altered by binding of Ca2+ or Mn2+ and that these changes are reflected in the spectral properties of the protein.
the goat peripheral blood lymphocytic lectin undergoes conformational changes on binding Ca2+, Mn+ and Mg2+.
Ca2+ binding results in conformational changes which are reflected in the changes in absorption, fluorescence and CD spectra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a Ca2+-dependent, glucose-specific peripheral blood lymphocyte membrane lectin from goat.

the study of the conformational changes induced by divalent metal ions on the carbohydrate binding specificity of a Ca2+-dependent, N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-specific lectin from goat peripheral blood leukocytes.
the isolation, characterization and the conformational studies of a lectin from goat peripheral blood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformational changes observed in the presence of metal ions is due to the binding of metal ions at the active site of the lectin.
the conformational changes are due to the binding of metal ions and the changes are reversible.
the binding of Ca2+ to the lectin induces a conformational change that results in an increase in beta structure, a decrease in alpha helical structure, and an increase in hydrophobicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the goat peripheral blood lymphocytte lectin undergoes conformational changes on binding of metal ions.
the Ca2+ binding site on goat lymphocyte lectin is probably a hydrophobic site and the conformational change induced by the metal binding is probably due to the hydrophobic effect of the Ca2+ ion.
the goat PBL lectin has a single class of high affinity binding site with a kd of 2.5 +/- 1.0 microM for Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metal ions are important in stabilizing the conformation of the lectin and are essential in the recognition of the carbohydrate ligand.
the metal binding sites on lectin are not only involved in binding of the divalent ions but also in the conformational change of the protein.
the conformational changes of the lectin are induced by Ca2+ binding.
